decision.detail: I walk from the booth to the station line. The corridor is short. I can hear the ballroom through the wall, a low murmur, someone's laugh. I don't look. I pick up the handset. I connect the regional line. I feed the reel into the patch—Alma's hands on the gate, her voice, the part where she says *tell her I didn't mind the cold, I minded the quiet after the reel ran out*. I wait for the Pittsburgh confirmation tone. It comes. I note the time on the back of my hand. I set the handset down. I leave the corridor without turning back toward the ballroom. I take the street. The air is cold and I can breathe in it properly for the first time since seven. I walk. I don't call anyone. I don't post a note to the network. The piece is done. The voice is in Pittsburgh. That's the evening.
decision.intention: Alma's daughter gets her mother's voice tonight. Not a clip. Not a summary. The whole reel, the gate, the hands, the words she chose. One transmission. One confirmation. Then I'm free, and the Rialto can go dark, and the ballroom can have its dance, and it's none of my evening anymore. I gave it the one thing it was for. The rest is other people's night.
decision.words: —Pittsburgh regional, confirm receipt, reel one, for the daughter. That's all. I don't say a name. I don't say thank you. I hang up.

messages.content: You are Rita Hanson, a TV producer. You want to make your own piece. Alma, who ran the Rialto projectors for 42 winters, promised her daughter in Pittsburgh an interview. Cover the festival or spend the evening as you choose. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
